audit_status.review_note: Reviewed as Eliphaz's opening response: rebuke framed as counsel, retribution logic, harvest metaphor, night vision, and mortal impurity argument. Claims are preserved as Eliphaz's speech, not endorsed as the book's final theology.

verses.restored: Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:

familiar.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

modern.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

original.text: וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: If one attempts a word with you, will you be weary? But who can hold back from speaking?

familiar.text: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?

modern.text: “If one ventures a word with you, will you be wearied? Yet who can keep from speaking?

original.text: הֲנִסָּ֬ה דָבָ֣ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ תִּלְאֶ֑ה וַעְצֹ֥ר בְּ֝מִלִּ֗ין מִ֣י יוּכָֽל

verses.restored: Look, you have instructed many, and weak hands you have strengthened.

familiar.text: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.

modern.text: Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.

original.text: הִ֭נֵּה יִסַּ֣רְתָּ רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדַ֖יִם רָפ֣וֹת תְּחַזֵּֽק

verses.restored: Your words have raised up the stumbling, and bending knees you have made firm.

familiar.text: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.

modern.text: Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.

original.text: כּ֭וֹשֵׁל יְקִימ֣וּן מִלֶּ֑יךָ וּבִרְכַּ֖יִם כֹּרְע֣וֹת תְּאַמֵּֽץ

verses.restored: But now it comes to you, and you are weary; it touches you, and you are terrified.

familiar.text: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.

modern.text: But now trouble has come upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are dismayed.

original.text: כִּ֤י עַתָּ֨ה תָּב֣וֹא אֵלֶ֣יךָ וַתֵּ֑לֶא תִּגַּ֥ע עָ֝דֶ֗יךָ וַתִּבָּהֵֽל

verses.restored: Is not your fear your confidence, and your hope the integrity of your ways?

familiar.text: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?

modern.text: Is your reverence not your confidence, and the uprightness of your ways your hope?

original.text: הֲלֹ֣א יִ֭רְאָתְךָ כִּסְלָתֶ֑ךָ תִּ֝קְוָתְךָ֗ וְתֹ֣ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Remember, please: who that was innocent has perished? And where were the upright cut off?

familiar.text: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?

modern.text: Consider now, I plead: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?

original.text: זְכָר נָ֗א מִ֤י ה֣וּא נָקִ֣י אָבָ֑ד וְ֝אֵיפֹ֗ה יְשָׁרִ֥ים נִכְחָֽדוּ

verses.restored: As I have seen, those who plow trouble and sow harm harvest it.

familiar.text: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.

modern.text: As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap the same.

original.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָ֭אִיתִי חֹ֣רְשֵׁי אָ֑וֶן וְזֹרְעֵ֖י עָמָ֣ל יִקְצְרֻֽהוּ

verses.restored: By the breath of the Divine they perish, and by the wind of his nostrils they are consumed.

familiar.text: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.

modern.text: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.

original.text: מִנִּשְׁמַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וּמֵר֖וּחַ אַפּ֣וֹ יִכְלֽוּ

verses.restored: The roar of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of young lions are broken.

familiar.text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

modern.text: The lion may roar, and the fierce lion may growl, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.

original.text: שַׁאֲגַ֣ת אַ֭רְיֵה וְק֣וֹל שָׁ֑חַל וְשִׁנֵּ֖י כְפִירִ֣ים נִתָּֽעוּ

verses.restored: The strong lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

familiar.text: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion’s whelps are scattered abroad.

modern.text: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

original.text: לַ֭יִשׁ אֹבֵ֣ד מִבְּלִי טָ֑רֶף וּבְנֵ֥י לָ֝בִ֗יא יִתְפָּרָֽדוּ

verses.restored: A word was stolen secretly to me, and my ear received a whisper of it.

familiar.text: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.

modern.text: Now a word came to me secretly; my ears caught a whisper of it.

original.text: וְ֭אֵלַי דָּבָ֣ר יְגֻנָּ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֥ח אָ֝זְנִ֗י שֵׁ֣מֶץ מֶֽנְהֽוּ

verses.restored: In thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people,

familiar.text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,

modern.text: In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

original.text: בִּ֭שְׂעִפִּים מֵחֶזְיֹנ֣וֹת לָ֑יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֥ל תַּ֝רְדֵּמָ֗ה עַל אֲנָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: dread met me, and trembling, and made the multitude of my bones shake.

familiar.text: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.

modern.text: fear and trembling came over me and made all my bones shudder.

original.text: פַּ֣חַד קְ֭רָאַנִי וּרְעָדָ֑ה וְרֹ֖ב עַצְמוֹתַ֣י הִפְחִֽיד

verses.restored: A spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh bristled.

familiar.text: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:

modern.text: Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body bristled.

original.text: וְ֭רוּחַ עַל פָּנַ֣י יַחֲלֹ֑ף תְּ֝סַמֵּ֗ר שַֽׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּשָׂרִֽי

verses.restored: It stood still, but I did not recognize its appearance; a form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice:

familiar.text: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,

modern.text: It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form loomed before my eyes, and I heard a whispering voice:

original.text: יַעֲמֹ֤ד וְֽלֹא אַכִּ֬יר מַרְאֵ֗הוּ תְּ֭מוּנָה לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י דְּמָמָ֖ה וָק֣וֹל אֶשְׁמָֽע

verses.restored: Can a mortal be more righteous than the Divine? Can a strong man be more pure than his Maker?

familiar.text: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?

modern.text: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?

original.text: הַֽ֭אֱנוֹשׁ מֵאֱל֣וֹהַ יִצְדָּ֑ק אִ֥ם מֵ֝עֹשֵׂ֗הוּ יִטְהַר גָּֽבֶר

verses.restored: Look, he puts no trust in his servants, and against his messengers he charges error.

familiar.text: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:

modern.text: If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error,

original.text: הֵ֣ן בַּ֭עֲבָדָיו לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וּ֝בְמַלְאָכָ֗יו יָשִׂ֥ים תָּהֳלָֽה

verses.restored: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in dust, who are crushed before the moth.

familiar.text: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?

modern.text: how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who can be crushed like a moth!

original.text: אַ֤ף שֹׁכְנֵ֬י בָֽתֵּי חֹ֗מֶר אֲשֶׁר בֶּעָפָ֥ר יְסוֹדָ֑ם יְ֝דַכְּא֗וּם לִפְנֵי עָֽשׁ

verses.restored: Between morning and evening they are beaten down; without anyone noticing, they perish forever.

familiar.text: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.

modern.text: They are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk; unnoticed, they perish forever.

original.text: מִבֹּ֣קֶר לָעֶ֣רֶב יֻכַּ֑תּוּ מִבְּלִ֥י מֵ֝שִׂ֗ים לָנֶ֥צַח יֹאבֵֽדוּ

verses.restored: Is not their tent-cord pulled up within them? They die, and not with wisdom.

familiar.text: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.

modern.text: Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’

original.text: הֲלֹא נִסַּ֣ע יִתְרָ֣ם בָּ֑ם יָ֝מ֗וּתוּ וְלֹ֣א בְחָכְמָֽה
